finish.text:
Done. The cheapest available item in the Electronics category was added to the cart: 'USB-C Charging Cable 6ft' by CableTech (product_320), price $7.99, quantity 1.

How each requirement was met:
1) Electronics category browsed - opened via 'Browse Electronics'; the listing URL carried category=Electronics with 47 results, and the product page breadcrumb reads Home > Electronics > Chargers & Power Adapters.
2) Cheapest available identified - the category results were sorted with the site's own 'Price: Low to High' control across all 47 results; this cable was the first card and is labelled 'In Stock' with 'Ships from and sold by Amazon.com'. The next card, '2 Pack Portable Charger' at $15.00, is labelled 'Currently unavailable', so it was excluded. Every other readable price on the first results page was $15.00 or higher.
3) Added to cart - the Add to Cart button produced an 'Added to Cart - USB-C Charging Cable 6ft' confirmation, the header badge went from '0 items' to '1 items', and the cart page (/env/amazon/cart) now shows exactly one line item: 'USB-C Charging Cable 6ft', 7.99, quantity 1, Subtotal (1 item): 7.99.

Membership witness: prepare_link_membership was run before the cart change on the product detail page (entity_indices [0], readback on the Cart link) and returned baseline matching_links 0; verify_link_membership after the change returned 'new_link_membership_observed' with matching_links 1 and same_label_other_urls 0. The witness is reported only as evidence of cart membership, not as evidence of cheapest-selection or of full task correctness - those are supported separately by the sort ordering, the In Stock label, and the cart line item.

Limits worth knowing: the exact dollar amount was not readable in the listing or detail price markup (the price block rendered as empty dollar spans plus a cents fragment); $7.99 comes from the cart page text. And 'cheapest' rests on the site's price-ascending sort over the whole category rather than on a manual comparison of all 47 prices.
